data.character: Modern 15-storey commercial/office tower with contrasting faces: one highly reflective dark blue-green curtain-wall side carrying a large circular clock/graphic feature, and other sides made of a pale silver-white metal-panel frame with regular blue glass office windows. The tower has a narrow light-clad service/core strip with only sparse small openings, plus a more transparent office grid and glazed lower floors.

levels.note: Ground and low podium levels are mostly full-height blue-green glass with light silver/white framing. On the clock/feature facade this reads as very dark reflective curtain wall; on the street-front office side it is a large glazed storefront/office wall with horizontal sign bands.

Main occupied tower floors. The typical office elevations have a regular grid of blue tinted glazing set in broad pale silver-white metal-panel spandrels and mullion bands, roughly one horizontal band per floor. One side is a continuous darker reflective glass curtain wall; another has an oval/circular metal rim with red clock-like beams and red projecting box accents over the glass. A narrow vertical core/side bay is mostly pale panel cladding with a thin vertical dark-glass slot and a few small punched windows.

Upper crown/mechanical and top office zone becomes brighter and more silvery in daylight. It keeps the same glass-and-panel rhythm on office faces, with pale metal-clad parapet/crown edges and a rooftop guardrail. The service-core strip remains mostly light metal panel with sparse narrow openings and signage near the top.

data.notes: Colours follow the measured samples: dark reflective lower/mid glass reads blue-green grey, while upper and trim areas read pale blue-silver. The building is not windowless: most faces have regular curtain-wall or window-wall office glazing. However, some side/core surfaces are nearly blank light metal panel with only small slit or punched openings. Use the regular office grid on unphotographed occupied elevations, but include at least one dark reflective curtain-wall feature face if modelling the whole tower.
